Build Discipline Packet

Written and committed before any Week 6 code (a457cd0, approved by the owner at Gate 1).

🧩 Problem: what user problem is this feature solving?

A freelancer keeps their work in their head: which invoice is late, whether the deposit landed, when the next deadline is, and what they can expect to earn next month. FreeFlow already answers those questions, but a visitor can't tell. The signed-out landing page is a list of features, the top bar holds eight links and Week 6 adds more, and the evidence of how the product was built (seven weeks of research, pricing, tests and decisions) is spread across files only the grader reads.

The venture problem underneath: FreeFlow has to prove it works, creates value and avoids obvious harm, and it has to show a visitor that it was built by listening to freelancers, with intention, rather than claim it. That means one story a stranger can follow, one way to move around the whole site, and open numbers and sources instead of testimonials.

👤 User: who will use it?

UserNeed
A freelancer landing on FreeFlow for the first time (designer, photographer, video editor, writer, developer)Recognise their own late-night worries, see that each one has a real answer, try it for free, or ask to hear about the lifetime version
An existing FreeFlow userGet to their dashboard and every tool from any page, quickly, on a phone
The course graderFind every Module 6 requirement (see the map above) without being told where it is
Brayden, the ownerMeasure the funnel (try-free clicks, launch-list sign-ups), hear from users, and keep his promise to keep listening and fixing

🎯 Success: what must work by the end of the week?

/demo loads for anyone, signed in or out, with no AI key and with the database unreachable, and a first-time visitor can follow it from 11:47 pm to morning without instructions, on phone and desktop. Every page carries the Dock. /dashboard shows the signed-in user's own records and a public "FreeFlow in public" tab of counts. /docs holds the journey (agent map), the week-by-week build log, the prompt library, the testing summary, the impact check and the V2 roadmap with votes. Try-free clicks and launch-list sign-ups are recorded. Nothing on any new page states a price, names an unbuilt feature on /demo, or invents a testimonial or count. All automated suites pass, five external users have walked through /demo → sign-up → dashboard → docs, at least one bug they found is fixed and redeployed, and the full-site regression passes.

Implementation note. /demo is one long scroll in the founder's voice, built on AIDA: Attention (11:47 pm, sorting the worries), Interest (midnight, the guided walkthrough of real features), story (1 am, the signed founder story), Desire (the "You said → we changed" proof), the game as the climax, and Action (8:00 am, try it free or join the launch list). The worries in chapter 1 are the features in chapter 2 and the upgrades in the game, so the page is one story rather than a stack of sections. The job picker re-colours the accent and swaps the examples throughout. Motion is CSS and small hand-written code; under reduced motion each chapter shows its calm end state. The Dock replaces the top bar's links on every page. /dashboard and /docs read the same static content modules as /demo, so the same features, voice and numbers appear everywhere.

✂️ Scope Cut: what looked nice but will not be built this week?

From the spec's non-goals:

  • Game leaderboard and the "free lifetime access" prize (they wait until scores can be protected from cheating)
  • A private owner analytics view (the owner already sees emails and chats in Supabase)
  • A founder photo, and the before/after photo hover
  • Any change to /pricing content or to the pricing model beyond the two fixes above
  • Any V2 roadmap item (simpler forecast, CFDI, more countries/languages/currencies, studio accounts, etc.)
  • Paid APIs of any kind

🏗 Architecture: frontend, backend, database, data flow

Static content modules (typed TypeScript, in the repo, one source each)
  lib/funnel/*   jobs + accents, worries, walkthrough steps, story, copy
  lib/venture/*  "You said → we changed" changes, roadmap, journey, timeline,
                 prompts, testing (bugs found/fixed)
  lib/game/engine.ts   pure game logic (tick, age, collect, upgrades, score)
        │ read by
        ▼
Pages (Next.js App Router)
  /demo  (also / signed out)  ── DemoFunnel: chapters 1–6, game, sticky CTA
  /dashboard                  ── "Your work" (existing dashboard) + PublicNumbers
  /docs                       ── JourneyStepper, WeekTimeline, PromptLibrary,
                                 TestingSummary, ImpactCheck, Roadmap
  every page                  ── <Dock /> in app/layout.tsx
        │ anonymous writes (rate-limited, zod-validated)
        ▼
  POST /api/funnel         { event, job?, visitId }    → funnel_events
  POST /api/launch-list    { email, consent, source }  → launch_list
  POST /api/roadmap/vote   { itemId, voterKey }        → roadmap_votes
        │ insert-only RLS, no select policy on any of them
        ▼
Supabase (Postgres)
  funnel_events · launch_list · roadmap_votes · count_exclusions (owner-filled)
  venture_counts()  security definer → JSON of totals only
        │ read via supabase.rpc("venture_counts")
        ▼
  "FreeFlow in public" tab (/dashboard)  and  vote counts (/docs roadmap)

Signed-in records (unchanged): /dashboard "Your work" → existing projects table (RLS per account)
Routing: proxy.ts (Next.js 16) · / signed in → /dashboard · / signed out → funnel
No database or AI key → /demo still works fully; writes answer 503 { saved: false }

⚙️ DevOps: GitHub, Vercel, Supabase, env variables, deployment plan

Work on branch week6. GitHub main deploys to Vercel production (https://www.freeflow.website); each push to the branch gets a preview. Environment variables are unchanged: no new keys. The migration supabase/week6_venture.sql is run by the owner in the Supabase SQL Editor; it is idempotent, never drops a table and ends with a verify block. Until it is run, the write routes answer 503 and the public counts show as unavailable, which is the designed degraded state. Each push is gated on exit codes: npm test, npm run lint, npm run build, then npx tsc --noEmit. At least 5 commits and 2 Vercel deployments: the first after the full-site regression, the second after fixing a bug the external testers found.

🧪 Test Plan: how will you verify it works?

  • Automated (npm test, npm run test:chat): venture content integrity (every change cites an existing file, roadmap ids unique, journey has seven steps, prompts have weeks); funnel content per job (every walkthrough step is a built feature, five jobs, accents from the brand); game engine (timer, ageing, collection, each upgrade's effect, scoring, winnability, long-tick clamp); schemas (email normalisation, consent, unknown item, unknown event); route source checks (rate limit before parsing, 503 with no client, 23505 as success, never .select(); UI source checks (real buttons, storage wrapped in try/catch, canonical link, no price strings, no friend names).
  • Live checks: every page signed out, signed in, and at 375 px, including the Dock on each; /demo with the database unreachable; / signed in and out; a real launch-list sign-up and a repeat; a vote and a repeat; the public tab with no personal data.
  • Full-site regression: all automated suites plus the live checks above, recorded in docs/week6/TEST_EVIDENCE.md.
  • 5 external users (recruited by the owner): each walks /demo → sign-up → dashboard → docs. Only what really happened is recorded, in docs/week6/EXTERNAL_TESTS.md, with no names. At least one bug they find is fixed, tested and redeployed, and logged in docs/week6/ITERATION_LOG.md.

🤖 Coding Agent Prompt: exact prompt to Claude Code

Implement docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-09-week6-integrated-venture.md task by task against the spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-09-week6-integrated-venture-design.md, and build only the agreed scope in docs/week6/PLAN.md. Before writing route, layout, metadata or font code, read the relevant guide in node_modules/next/dist/docs/: this is Next.js 16 and route protection lives in proxy.ts. Test first for every pure module (content, funnel, game, schemas) and keep npm test, npm run lint, npm run build and npx tsc --noEmit green. Match the feel of the validated prototypes in .superpowers/brainstorm/*/content/ and use app/globals.css as the only source of colour. Never state a price on a new page, never name an unbuilt feature on /demo, never invent a testimonial, count, rating, logo or "You said → we changed" entry, and keep friends and testers unnamed. Every animation needs a calm reduced-motion version, every interaction must work by keyboard and touch at 375 px, and /demo must work with no AI key and no database. Add no paid service and no runtime dependency without a one-line reason. Never handle the Supabase secret key: the owner runs supabase/week6_venture.sql. The course coding tasks map onto the plan as: integrate all pages (Tasks 6 and 9: the Dock and / routing), create /dashboard (Task 7), create /demo (Tasks 9–12), create agent map (Task 8, the journey stepper), create testing summary (Tasks 8 and 15), create version 2 roadmap (Tasks 2, 5 and 8).

Iteration Log: What Changed After Testing

1. A fresh code review of the whole site before release

Four problems a visitor would hit, each fixed with a test that failed first:

  • Hovering opened the Dock and moved its button, so a click aimed at the button opened a page instead. Page icons now wait a moment before taking a click.
  • A dragged worry stuttered because its shake animation fought the drag. Dragging now stops the shake.
  • On phones, the worry panel blocked scrolling the page. Only the worries block it now.
  • Three help-desk answers still described the old top bar and said FreeFlow sends no other email. They now match the site.

Three smaller findings were re-graded by their effect and fixed too: the first tap after a drag was ignored, a game round could be counted twice in the public numbers, and long worries were cut off on phones.

2. The owner's own review

  • The founder story said it was built "for a class". It now says it was built by choice.
